name: arc-uniform-line-marking
description: Use when ARC grids contain near-uniform full rows and columns. Identify full-length marker lines and recolor them consistently.
---

# ARC: Marking full-length uniform lines

Use this pattern when an ARC input has a noisy two-color field, but some entire rows or columns are uniformly one color (or nearly so).

1. Inspect row and column profiles for full-width/full-height uniform lines. Treat the continuous long stripe structure as significant; isolated anomalous cells in a stripe may be noise.
2. Use a demonstration to identify the target output color and whether to transform only full-length lines or also near-uniform lines. Preserve all other cells exactly.
3. Recolor each identified full row/column to the demonstrated marker color. Where a row and column intersect, the same replacement naturally applies.
4. Verify dimensions and compare the resulting grid cell-by-cell against the input outside the marked lines.

## Known solved pattern (task-e1473598)

The marker color was 2. In a 28x9 input with recurring vertical color-6 stripes in columns 2 and 5 (zero-based), and full-width color-6 separator rows, recolor those two columns and all full-width color-6 rows to 2. Preserve the irregular cells elsewhere, including isolated 6s that do not belong to the full-length stripes/separator rows. A demonstration of the same pattern showed long horizontal and vertical uniform marker lines recolored to 2 while all other cells remained unchanged.

This is a pattern heuristic, not a universal ARC rule: confirm line selection and output color from demonstrations when available.",
